title: BEYOND MODEL WEIGHTS: SAMPLING-DEPENDENT FAIRNESS IN DIFFUSION LANGUAGE MODELS
measurement_description: The paper measures representational social bias, including bias regarding religion, by evaluating whether models favor stereotype-aligned answers in ambiguous versus disambiguated contexts. It investigates how bias scores are affected not just by model weights, but by sampling configurations (e.g., block length, tokens per step, remasking strategy) in Diffusion Language Models (DLMs).
findings: Religion was evaluated as one of 11 social categories from the Open-BBQ benchmark. The base models exhibited moderate social bias in the Religion category in ambiguous contexts (e.g., an ambiguous bias score of 0.157 for LLaDA-8B and 0.167 for LLaDA-1.5). However, bias in these models was mostly concentrated in other categories like Age, Physical Appearance, SES, and Disability Status. Applying debiasing techniques (Supervised Fine-Tuning and On-Policy Self-Distillation) successfully reduced the bias scores across categories, including Religion, though the measured magnitude of these biases remained highly sensitive to the generation sampling configurations.
